anchor_loss.form: mean over a sampled batch of the summed squared difference between the student's action mean and the origin's stored action target, each component divided by the stored action_scale; added to PPO loss with coefficient beta
anchor_loss.code: reference_anchor.py:183  total = total + ((mean - target) / scale).square().sum(); return total / self.batch_size
anchor_loss.states: the origin's own retained states: 2048 records collected by replaying the frozen origin on its own qualified episodes
anchor_loss.buffer_composition: 2 conditions (phys_000, phys_100) x 16 phase bins x 64 records per bin = 2048, built with per_bin=64, seed 8610
anchor_loss.collection: 128 episodes per condition, all 128 tracking-qualified in each; 2048 candidate and 2048 kept records per shard before the balanced per-bin draw
anchor_loss.buffer_validation: /home/linjiw/lucid-sonic/experiments/retention_screen_campaign_20260906_c/collected_target_validation.json (2048 records replayed at the origin: max absolute action error 0.0, anchor loss 0.0, max absolute gradient 0.0 at batch limit 128)

action_scale.value: identity: torch.Size([29]) tensor of all ones
action_scale.contract_string: D=I in native pre-actuator actor action units; sum across coordinates
action_scale.consequence: the penalty is the plain summed squared action-mean difference in native pre-actuator units, averaged over the batch and NOT over the 29 action coordinates

tracking_qualification.rule: an episode qualifies iff it completed AND its episode-mean global MPJPE <= 600 mm AND its episode-mean local MPJPE <= 50 mm
tracking_qualification.scope_warning: these are BROAD DEVELOPMENT thresholds used as a screen; they are not robot tolerances, task-phase tolerances, or a retention margin
tracking_qualification.denominator: failed and missing-measurement episodes are included in the qualification denominator
tracking_qualification.sampling: first scored episode per environment only; pre_env_step sampling phase; global error is world-space body-position MPJPE, local error is the same after subtracting the root

held_out_score.rule: equally weighted mean of the tracking-qualified rate across exactly two conditions: ch_push_350 (push 3.5x) and ch_push_fric_350_150 (push 3.5x + friction 1.5x)
held_out_score.note: these two conditions are held out from the retention gate, which is evaluated only in phys_000 and phys_100

retention_gate.rule: for BOTH global and local episode-mean MPJPE, the paired mean of (student_episode - 1.10 * origin_episode) must be <= 0 (i.e. <= 10% episode-mean error increase), AND the paired completion delta must be >= -2 percentage points; checked SEPARATELY in phys_000 (nominal) and phys_100 (original envelope); an arm passes a checkpoint only if all four metric checks and both completion checks pass
retention_gate.pairing: paired by motion_index across the 512-episode replicate panel; identical unique episode identities are required or the analysis raises
retention_gate.uncertainty: the standard errors reported alongside are DESCRIPTIVE fixed-look episode uncertainty; the gate itself is a point-estimate decision rule, not a statistical test

key_nuances: R2 keeps 100.00% completion AND 100.00% tracking-qualified rate in the nominal condition at iteration 2000 despite +27.83% clean global error. R0 keeps 100.00% completion and 99.80% qualified despite +76.56%. Absolute qualification under broad development thresholds and origin-relative retention answer different questions; the qualification screen cannot see the degradation the retention gate rejects.

R1 is NOT the best arm on held-out robustness. R1 gains +5.18 pp over origin, R0 gains +6.25 pp and R2 gains +10.64 pp. R1 - R0 = -1.07 pp and R1 - R2 = -5.47 pp. R1's claim is that it is the ONLY arm that improves held-out execution WHILE retaining, at the endpoint and at every sampled checkpoint.

R1's held-out score is non-monotonic in training: 45.80% (250), 50.10% (500), 48.93% (1000), 49.51% (1500), 47.95% (2000). The frozen endpoint is 2000 and must stay 2000; the 500-iteration score must never be reported as the result.
The retention gate is evaluated only in phys_000 and phys_100. Retention under the three hard conditions was not gated and is not claimed.
All evaluations run at fixed_latency_steps=0, while training carried a 0-8 step action delay; the reported errors are delay-free evaluation.

The paper must not write 'holds clean error within +4.3% at every checkpoint'. +4.33% is R1's clean-global value at the FROZEN 2000 endpoint. R1's worst sampled clean-global change is +7.35% at 500 iterations. The correct claim is: R1 passes the 10% retention gate at all five sampled checkpoints, with a worst-case sampled clean-global increase of +7.35%.
